Article Title: India to take on Pakistan in high-stakes Hockey World Cup clash
Article Text:
Harmanpreet Singh (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

An India-Pakistan contest in any sport evokes emotions that often go beyond competitiveness. There was a phase in hockey when beating the arch-rivals was celebrated almost like winning a trophy.None of the current crop of Indian players has faced Pakistan in a hockey World Cup before. But they have someone in their corner who knows exactly what such a contest entails. Shivendra Singh , a formidable striker of his generation known as much for his style as his flair with the stick, featured in the last World Cup meeting between the two sides in New Delhi in 2010, which India won 4-1.At the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, Netherlands, the teams will renew their rivalry in a crucial encounter, and Shivendra’s experience could prove invaluable as he helps the players navigate the contest’s emotional intensity.Skipper Harmanpreet Singh stressed the importance of keeping emotions in check on Wednesday after India’s 2-4 loss to England.“We made some silly mistakes, and there are lots of learnings from this match. Against Pakistan, it is important for us to keep our emotions under control,” said the ace drag-flicker.India will start as favourites against a Pakistan side that has struggled to regain even a fraction of its glorious past. Ranked 12th in the world, Pakistan have slipped from being a dominant force to also-rans.Lack of funds, limited scientific and match exposure, federation politics and an inability to keep pace with the changing demands of the game have all contributed to their decline.For the record, India are unbeaten in their last 19 matches against Pakistan, a run stretching back a decade.Their most recent meeting, in the FIH Pro League in June, saw India recover from a one-goal deficit to hammer Pakistan 7-1. That result should provide Harmanpreet and his men with confidence, though a World Cup knockout-like pressure will make Wednesday’s contest a different proposition.The equation is simple. India, with three points from two games, need at least a draw to advance. Pakistan, who lost to England and drew with Wales, must win to stay alive in the tournament.
Article Summary: India face Pakistan in their second World Cup match on Wednesday. India are unbeaten in their last 19 matches against Pakistan, a run stretching back a decade. Pakistan have slipped from being a dominant force to also-rans. India, with three points from two games, need at least a draw to advance.

Article Title: How Bangladesh beat lure of white-ball riches to save its Tests
Article Text:
The Test win in Darwin is the realisation of the talent and the immaculate process focusing on Test cricket put in place by the BCB.

Changing pitches in domestic cricket

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hiring legends as fast bowling coaches

Days before the Darwin Test against Bangladesh, Australia captain Pat Cummins had said in a podcast: “Some of our guys are saying no to half-a-million pounds for 20 days’ work to go and play those two Test matches against Bangladesh. I think it is a tension point. At the moment our guys are so keen to play for Australia that they’re happy to forgo that, but I don’t think we can accept that that is going to be the case forever.’”Cummins, the proud face of arguably the best fast-bowling attack in Tests today, was only reminding us aloud how the dynamics of world cricket have drastically changed over the last decade. But, it was Bangladesh cricket that quietly chose to go the other way during that period, a move that ironically culminated in mowing down Cummins’ powerhouse Test team on their own soil on Sunday.In doing so, six months after forfeiting their T20 World Cup place due to diplomatic reasons, they have made this World Test Championship cycle the most exciting one since its inception in 2019.Bangladesh’s pace resources have now become the talk of the cricket town. They had shown their potential in demolishing Pakistan — both at home and away in last two years.The Test win in Darwin is the realisation of the talent and the immaculate process focusing on Test cricket put in place by the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB).“Even (as recently as) fivesix years ago, pacers didn’t want to play Test cricket. They were happy playing just whiteball cricket. The BCB decided to incentivise Test cricket. Special contracts were drawn where the pacers could make a fancy living by playing Tests,” former Bangladesh captain and current chief selector Habibul Bashar, who led the team when Bangladesh beat Australia in an ODI for the first time in 2005, told TOI from Darwin.BCB changed the match fee and contract structure in 2019. Till then, ODI players were the best paid which resulted in fast bowlers backing out of Test cricket.The board decided to rework the contracts in a way that saw Test players become the highest paid cricketers in the country. The fee for a Test match has been doubled from 4 lakh Bangladeshi Taka to 8 lakh Bangladeshi Taka.“Now, our fast bowlers preserve themselves for Test cricket. They don’t run after contracts in T20 leagues. If a T20 league contract comes, the BCB assesses if the player can be released,” said Bashar.Now, Bangladesh have a battery of pacers who come from humble backgrounds. Tearaway quick Nahid Rana comes from a remote village in Rajshahi close to the India border and Hasan Mahmud is from Lakshmipur in Chittagong while Ebadot Hossain and Tanzim Shakib are from Sylhet.The word in Bangladesh cricket is that they don’t want bowlers going the Mustafizur Rahman way who didn’t prioritise Test cricket for playing in T20 leagues.The trigger point in the pace revolution came in 2014-15.Over the last decade, former Bangladesh captain Akram Khan, Bashar and Minhajul Abedin got working on domestic cricket in various capacities like chief selector, head of cricket operations and BCB director.“The domestic pitches used to be bare and spinner-friendly. The teams would play three spinners and one pacer. We worked on the grounds and decided to make it a rule of having at least 6-mm grass on the pitches.“We also made it compulsory for teams to play three pacers in first-class matches. It encouraged these bowlers from the outskirts to bowl fast. When the pitches became pacer-friendly, teams organically started picking more pacers,” Bashar said.Bangladesh cricket’s primary pipeline is U-19 cricket. When fast bowlers are spotted at that level, the board takes over their journey.However, a big point in Bangladesh’s pace-bowling revolution has been hiring big international bowlers as fast bowling coaches.“We brought in Courtney Walsh, Heath Streak and Allan Donald as fast bowling coaches. Their presence with the national team made a huge difference.“At the same time, we encouraged domestic coaches to spend time with them too. That knowledge passed on and helped in shaping raw fast bowlers,” Bashar claimed, subtly highlighting their ecosystem’s unique thinking that is creating a reverse revolution in cricket.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's pace resources have now become the talk of the cricket town. The Test win in Darwin is the realisation of the talent and the immaculate process focusing on Test cricket put in place by the Bangladesh Cricket Board. The trigger point in the pace revolution came in 2014-15.

Article Title: 23 state equestrian bodies seek time-bound EFI elections, flag governance concerns
Article Text:
Equestrian Federation of India (EFI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: As many as 23 state and union territory equestrian associations have called for a time-bound election process to restore an elected and representative administration at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), amid growing concerns over the prolonged governance uncertainty in the sport.The associations met at a New Delhi hotel on Aug 15 and unanimously adopted four resolutions, covering EFI elections, the functioning of the Ad Hoc Committee, transparency in decision-making and the inclusion of equestrian sport in the National Games and Khelo India Youth Games.The meeting came against the backdrop of the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, and the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026. The participating associations said the continuing uncertainty was neither in the interests of Indian equestrian sport nor its athletes and urged the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) and the International Equestrian Federation (FEI) to intervene.The most significant demand was for the Ad Hoc Committee overseeing the EFI to announce a definite election schedule and complete the electoral process at the earliest.The associations pointed to a three-month timeline for elections after the committee's constitution, claiming that the deadline had lapsed on June 26 without a formal extension from either the Delhi High Court or the IOA.They also raised concerns over changes in the composition of the four-member Ad Hoc Committee, stating that at least two members had exited and replacements had not been named. The associations urged the sports ministry to direct the IOA to take responsibility for conducting the EFI elections in line with the applicable legal framework and recent court directions.Another resolution questioned the Ad Hoc Committee's authority to take policy decisions in areas such as selection criteria, allocation of events in the annual calendar and tournament or entry fees. The state bodies maintained that such policy matters fall within the domain of the EFI General Body and pointed out that no General Body meeting had been held since August 2024.The associations further demanded greater transparency, calling for the publication of minutes of meetings of the Ad Hoc Committee and any sub-committees constituted by it.The meeting also highlighted the sport's achievements and its struggle for greater recognition at the domestic level. Indian equestrian athletes have won 14 Asian Games medals — four gold, three silver and seven bronze — while the country secured five medals at the 2025 Asian Equestrian Championships, including one gold and four silver.Despite that record, the associations noted that equestrian sport has not been included in the National Games or Khelo India Youth Games. They urged the IOA to include the discipline in every edition of the National Games and the MYAS and Sports Authority of India to ensure its inclusion in every Khelo India Youth Games.The associations also proposed a seven-member sub-committee to represent state bodies before the MYAS, IOA and FEI. Representatives from Gujarat, Karnataka, Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand and Delhi were proposed for the panel.
Article Summary: As many as 23 state and union territory equestrian associations have called for a time-bound election process to restore an elected and representative administration at the Equestrian Federation of India. The associations met at a New Delhi hotel on Aug 15 and unanimously adopted four resolutions, covering EFI elections, the functioning of the Ad Hoc Committee, transparency in decision- making and the inclusion of equestrians in the National Games and Khelo India Youth Games.

Article Title: Maharashtra gymnastics body seeks financial clarity from GFI, cites licence fees, grants
Article Text:
Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Amateur Gymnastics Association (MAGA), an affiliated member of the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI), has sought detailed financial and accounting clarifications from the national federation, raising questions over the accounting of licence fees, govt grants and affiliation income for the financial year 2024-25.In a communication to GFI president Sudhir Mittal, the Maharashtra body has sought documentary records and reconciled financial figures, stressing that transparency is essential for a national sports federation handling membership and competition-related fees as well as government funds.Among the key issues flagged is the GFI's audited financial statement for the year ended March 31, 2025. MAGA has asked the federation to disclose which competent authority reviewed and approved the accounts and whether the audited financials were placed before and approved by the GFI General Body. It has also sought the minutes of any such meeting.Questions have also allegedly been raised over the appointment of Narender Singh & Co, chartered accountants, as statutory auditors for 2024-25, including the authority that made the appointment, the audit fee fixed and whether the appointment was approved by the General Body.A major point of contention is the absence of licence-fee income in the financial statement.MAGA alleged that GFI collected Rs 1,000 per gymnast as a licence fee for participation in national championships and says the Maharashtra association facilitated payments for more than 220 gymnasts across disciplines and age groups. It has sought details of the total licence fees collected during 2024-25 and their utilisation.The association has similarly sought clarification over the apparent absence of affiliation-fee income and govt assistance from the income-and-expenditure account. It has asked for details of grants and financial assistance received from the Sports Authority of India and the union sports ministry, along with their accounting and utilisation.MAGA has also sought details of the GFI Finance Committee, including its present composition and the authority under which it was constituted, besides information on mechanisms to disclose conflicts of interest and related-party transactions involving office-bearers, executive committee members or their relatives.The development comes against the backdrop of a Feb 2026 show-cause notice issued to GFI by the ministry. The ministry had cited repeated delays in submission of proposals and utilisation certificates relating to govt grants, failure to empanel qualified coaches and support staff, inadequate planning for foreign exposure and national coaching camps, and complaints alleging non-transparent and unfair athlete-selection processes.GFI was asked to explain within 15 days why action under the Sports Code should not be taken.MAGA, while saying its latest communication is not intended to prejudge any office-bearer, has asked GFI to acknowledge the request and provide a timeline for furnishing the information. It warned that failure to respond could prompt escalation of the matter to the appropriate authorities.The association has maintained that its demand is aimed at financial accountability and transparency, particularly in view of the interests of athletes, coaches, state associations and other stakeholders in Indian gymnastics.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Amateur Gymnastics Association (MAGA) has sought detailed financial and accounting clarifications from the national federation. It has raised questions over the accounting of licence fees, govt grants and affiliation income for the financial year 2024-25. The development comes against the backdrop of a Feb 2026 show-cause notice issued to GFI.

Article Title: FIFA parts ways with COO Kevin Lamour after he criticised Infantino’s World Cup plan
Article Text:
UEFA's deputy general secretary Kevin Lamour, centre, (AP Photo)

Lamour criticised Infantino’s plan

FIFA confirms Lamour's departure

World Cup commercial plan abandoned

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: FIFA has parted ways with its Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour, days after he publicly criticised President Gianni Infantino’s controversial proposal to sell a stake in the governing body’s World Cup business.According to BBC Sport, FIFA confirmed that its working relationship with Lamour ended on August 17, 2026, after two years. The governing body said it thanked him for his service and wished him well for the future. The development comes after Lamour strongly opposed Infantino’s now-abandoned plan to create a commercial subsidiary linked to the World Cup and offer a minority stake to outside investors.Infantino had proposed creating a $20 billion tournament subsidiary, reportedly known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), with plans to sell up to a 20% stake to private equity investors. Lamour publicly criticised the proposal and said FIFA’s administration had not been given enough information about the plan.He described it as "the project of one person" and argued that the organisation's focus should remain on serving football."Our mission - the mission of the hundreds of passionate, dedicated, and exemplary FIFA employees - is to serve football. A president must bring people together, unite them, and inspire them.Today, we are experiencing the opposite," Lamour had said.Lamour also appeared to accept that speaking out could cost him his position."If that means I lose my job, then so be it," he said. "I will understand and respect that decision. At least I'll sleep well tonight."A FIFA spokesperson told BBC Sport: "the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026. FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future."FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström also informed staff about the change in an internal communication.According to the letter, quoted by BBC Sport, FIFA said the decision followed "careful consideration"."Following recent discussions, FIFA and our Chief Operating Officer, Kevin Lamour, have agreed to part ways. This decision was made after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionally… I felt it was important that I personally provide you with this update, and I would like to express my gratitude to Kevin for these contributions and for his work and commitment on behalf of FIFA on a daily basis. I wish Kevin all the best for the future," it said.The proposed World Cup commercial structure faced significant opposition before Infantino ultimately abandoned the plan. Lamour's criticism came as concerns grew within and outside FIFA over the proposal and the way it had been handled. The dispute has added to scrutiny surrounding Infantino's leadership as FIFA prepares for its presidential election in March 2027.Lamour is not the only senior figure reportedly to have raised concerns over the proposal. Carlos Cordeiro, a senior adviser to Infantino, also resigned before the plan was withdrawn. The episode has further fuelled debate over Infantino's leadership and his plans for another term as FIFA president.
Article Summary: Kevin Lamour, FIFA's Chief Operating Officer, has left the organisation. Lamour publicly criticised President Gianni Infantino's controversial proposal to sell a stake in the governing body's World Cup business. FIFA confirms Lamour's departure after two years of service.

Article Title: Scotland confident of ending 12-year World Cup drought, coach Dawkins backs 2027 qualification
Article Text:
(IANS) Scotland men’s head coach Owen Dawkins

Scotland one step away from World Cup

'It would be a magnificent achievement'

Batting depth boosts Scotland

Dawkins welcomes selection headaches

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Scotland head coach Owen Dawkins is confident his side can end a 12-year wait and secure qualification for next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Scotland have featured in just three editions of the 50-over World Cup, with their most recent appearance coming in 2015. They went winless in all six matches in Australia and New Zealand that year.However, the Scots have taken a significant step towards returning to the global showpiece after securing their place in the 2027 World Cup Qualifier through their impressive campaign in the ongoing ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2.Scotland now need to finish among the top four at the Global Qualifier at the start of 2027 to book their place at the World Cup. Dawkins, who took charge as Scotland head coach at the end of last year, believes his team has enough quality and momentum to achieve the feat."We are in a good place just now," Dawkins told Cricket Scotland, as quoted by the ICC."This series has demonstrated the character and quality within this Scotland side.Securing qualification for the Global Qualifier is a significant achievement, and everyone involved can be proud of the progress we have made."Scotland's coach also stressed the importance of ODI cricket and said reaching the World Cup would be the pinnacle for the current group."ODI cricket remains a hugely important format for the global game, and it would be a magnificent achievement if we reached the World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia," Dawkins said."It would represent the pinnacle for us as a group. This is a format that we need and world cricket need to continue investing in to help our players develop and to enable our sport to grow, strengthen and thrive."Much of Scotland's success in League 2 has been driven by their batting unit. George Munsey , Brandon McMullen and captain Richie Berrington have all made important contributions as Scotland climbed to the top of the standings during their recent home tri-series against Canada and the UAE.McMullen has also provided valuable contributions with the ball, while young spinner Lyle Robertson made a huge impact on debut against Canada by claiming six wickets. The emergence of several players has created healthy competition for places ahead of the Global Qualifier.Dawkins believes the competition for places is a positive sign, particularly after several players produced standout performances during the recent series."There were some outstanding individual performances over the last fortnight. Fin McCreath scored his maiden international century, Richie Berrington produced a fantastic hundred in the final match, while Lyle Robertson enjoyed an amazing debut, with the fourth-best bowling figures in ODI cricket history," he said.However, Dawkins was more pleased with Scotland's collective performances than individual milestones."Two matches in the series went right down to the final few overs, while four of our last six victories have come in the closing stages of games," he said."That success is not down to luck, but from the skill levels within the squad, backed up by hard work, commitment and dedication shown by everyone involved," he said.
Article Summary: Scotland head coach Owen Dawkins is confident his side can qualify for the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Scotland have featured in just three editions of the 50-over World Cup, with their most recent appearance coming in 2015. The Scots have taken a significant step towards returning to the global showpiece after securing their place in the 20 27 World Cup Qualifier.

Article Title: Air of discontent: Anders Antonsen wants India Open moved out of Delhi winter
Article Text:
New Delhi: Denmark's Anders Antonsen (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Anders Antonsen has returned to Delhi with a victory — and a familiar warning for the Badminton World Federation (BWF): if the India Open remains in the capital’s winter months, he would rather pay the fine than breathe through another tournament.The Danish world No. 4, a four-time World Championships medallist, has skipped the India Open for the last three editions, including this year, and was fined $5,000 for his latest withdrawal. His objection, he stressed after beating Azerbaijan’s Dicky Dwi Pangestu 21-19, 21-17 at the ongoing Worlds on Monday, is not to Delhi but to its Jan-Feb air.“In Jan and Feb, the pollution here is quite insane. It’s not pleasant to play in. You kind of get this burning feeling in your throat,” Antonsen said. “Imagine having your pulse high and trying to fight for air. It’s not a pleasant feeling.”The contrast with Aug has only strengthened his argument. “If I was the BWF, I would host the India Open at another time of the year,” he said, adding that the conditions now are “way better”. "When I open the blinds in the morning, I can see stuff," he added.Antonsen has accepted that his stance could again cost him.“When I see the calendar, I’m like, okay, they’re all instantly giving me a $5,000 fine.”Mia Blichfeldt, meanwhile, finds herself in a different bind despite sharing concerns about Delhi’s conditions. The Dane, returning after knee problems, advanced with a 21-18, 21-4 win over Azerbaijan’s Keisha Fatimah Azzahra but cannot simply walk away from a Super 750.“No, I will not do that because I am not in the same position like him. It's the rankings...I can’t miss out playing a 750 tournament,” she said.Mia believes conditions are “better” now, allowing her to focus on performance. Antonsen can opt out; Mia cannot. Their message, however, is similar: Delhi may be manageable in summer, but winter pollution should not be part of the BWF season.
Article Summary: Anders Antonsen says he would rather pay a $5,000 fine than play another tournament in Delhi. The Danish world No. 4 has skipped the India Open for the last three editions. He beat Azerbaijan’s Dicky Dwi Pangestu 21-19, 21-17 at the ongoing Worlds on Monday.

Article Title: No Khel Ratna recommendation for 2025, 17 athletes get Arjuna Awards
Article Text:
Khel Ratna goes vacant; 17 athletes receive Arjuna Awards (Images: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, India’s highest sporting honour, will have no recipient for 2025, with the government not recommending any sportsperson for the prestigious award. It is only the third time since the award was instituted in 1991-92 that no athlete has been chosen, after similar instances in 2008 and 2014.The recommendations, cleared by the National Sports Awards selection committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice (Retd.) Arun Kumar Mishra, were sent to sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya for final assent. The sports ministry announced the National Sports Awards 2025 on Tuesday.The development comes after the possibility of compound archer Jyothi Surekha Vennam and India’s women’s World Cup-winning cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur and vice-captain Smriti Mandhana being considered for the Khel Ratna was discussed by the committee at its meeting in New Delhi on December 12, 2025. However, none of the names found their way into the final recommendations.TOI was the first to break the story on December 12, 2025.The issue of the two leading Indian women cricketers was discussed at length, with the absence of a specific points-based system to assess cricket performances being a factor. In such cases, the committee generally relies on nominations from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). No nominations were made for the two cricketers. Mohammed Shami was the last cricketer to receive the Khel Ratna, in 2023.The Khel Ratna, known as the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna until August 2021, carries a cash prize of Rs 25 lakh, a medallion and a citation.While the top honour remained vacant, 17 sportspersons were named for the Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in sports and games.The list includes athletics stars Tejaswin Shankar, Muhammed Ajmal V and Priyanka Goswami; badminton players Treesa Jolly and Pullela Gayatri Gopichand; boxers Narender; chess players Vidit Santosh Gujarathi and Divya Jitendra Deshmukh; deaf shooter Dhanush Srikanth; hockey players Lalremsiami and Rajkumar Pal; kabaddi players Surjeet and Pooja; para-shooter Rudransh Khandelwal; para-athlete Ekta Bhyan; rower Arvind Singh; and shooter Akhil Sheoran.Deshmukh’s selection comes in the wake of her historic triumph at the FIDE Women’s World Cup, where she became the first Indian woman to win the title. Shankar, meanwhile, has been recognised following his performances in athletics, including his silver medal at the 2023 Asian Games.The government has also conferred one Arjuna Award in the lifetime category on footballer I Arumainayagam.In the Dronacharya Awards, the regular category honours went to athletics coach Parveer Singh, boxing coach Chhote Lal Yadav and shooting coach Neha Nandkumar Chavan. The lifetime category honours went to boxing coach Dharmendra Singh Yadav and wrestling coach Virender Kumar.The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar for sports promotion and development has been awarded to Army Paralympic Node, Pune.The awards recognise sporting excellence, coaching contribution and promotion of sports. Applications were invited through an online portal, with sportspersons, coaches and entities permitted to self-apply. A large number of applications were received and assessed by the selection committee comprising eminent sportspersons, people with experience in sports journalism and sports administrators.
Article Summary: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, India's highest sporting honour, will have no recipient for 2025. It is only the third time since the award was instituted in 1991-92 that no athlete has been chosen. 17 sportspersons were named for the Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in sports and games.

Article Title: 4-2 defeat to England leaves India with no room for error against Pakistan
Article Text:
India lose 2-4 to England. (Pic credit: Hockey India)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Result: England: 4 (Nicolas Bandurak 14, 55; Stuart Rushmere 39; Henry Croft 43) bt India 2 (Harmanpreet Singh 17, Dilpreet Singh 25).

It took England striker Nicholas Bandurak nine years to graduate from the junior to the senior national team. In the intervening years, he spent plenty of time watching and learning from some of the best in the business. One player he followed keenly was Indian skipper Harmanpreet Singh On Monday at the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, Netherlands, the Englishman of Ukrainian roots turned tutor as India went from impressive to disastrous. The 33-year-old scored a field goal, converted a penalty corner and provided crucial assists, each a key lesson for the Indians.In their second Pool outing at the FIH World Cup, the men in saffron paid a heavy price for elementary mistakes, surrendering a 2-1 lead to lose 2-4. The loss left Craig Fulton’s men in a must-win situation in their final league fixture against Pakistan on Wednesday.As expected, the contest began as a tug-of-war, with the anchors and pullers on either side throwing everything into the battle. Abhishek and Jarmanpreet Singh made a couple of impressive early inroads, but failed to turn them into goals.Bandurak, who made his World Cup debut in India in 2023, broke the deadlock in the 14th minute.Stuart Rushmere, another of England’s standout performers, brought down a long pass from deep and fed Bandurak, who had already outfoxed the Indian defenders and positioned himself perfectly to finish.India pressed hard, but England’s midfielders made it difficult for them to find a way through. Two minutes into the second quarter, however, Harmanpreet restored parity, finding the top-left corner with surgical precision.The repeated attacks down the flanks finally paid off when Abhishek took Hardik Singh’s free hit in the striking circle. Dilpreet Singh applied a deft touch to put India ahead.India went into the half-time break with a 2-1 advantage.But the warning signs were already there. England quickly worked out India’s defensive ploy as the latter tried to protect their lead.With India rotating goalkeepers every quarter, HS Mohith returned after the break. England immediately put him under pressure, and the youngster left angles exposed. Amit Rohidas and Jugraj Singh also struggled in the backline, conceding penalty corners that allowed England to build momentum.Rushmere made India pay, equalising with an artistic reverse flick after a sweeping pass exposed a chink in the Indian defence.England thrived on aerial balls and Rushmere brought one of them down with precision before finding Henry Croft in front of Mohith. The ball was slotted home with little fuss to put England ahead in the 43rd minute.Five minutes before the final hoot, Bandurak put the result beyond doubt, converting a set piece with a low flick that went beyond the reach of last-quarter goalkeeper Suraj Karkera.
Article Summary: Nicolas Bandurak scored a field goal, converted a penalty corner and provided crucial assists. Stuart Rushmere made India pay, equalising with an artistic reverse flick after a sweeping pass exposed a chink in the Indian defence. Henry Croft slotted home with little fuss to put England ahead.

Article Title: Dilip Tirkey breaks silence on World Cup absence amid Hockey India controversy
Article Text:
New Delhi, July 31 (IANS) Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With Hockey India secretary general Bhola Nath Singh and embattled director general RK Srivastava currently in the Netherlands for the FIH World Cup, questions have been raised about HI president Dilip Tirkey's absence from the tournament.Ongoing controversies within the federation and his face-off with Srivastava over the jersey colour-change row have brought the former Indian skipper’s absence into focus. Putting the speculation to rest, Tirkey told TOI: “I had informed the Executive Board well in advance that I would not travel for the World Cup because of the next edition of the Hockey India League (HIL). The league is crucial for exposure and the growth of both men’s and women’s hockey in the country.“I could not have stayed away from the country for a long period,” he added.“In fact, on Monday, treasurer Sekar Manoharan and I met potential stakeholders in Mumbai. I would have loved to be in the Netherlands, but my presence here was more essential,” Tirkey said.The HIL, a franchise-based league, was revived in 2024 under Tirkey’s leadership after a seven-year hiatus. While the league has attracted some of the top stars from around the world, it has also faced a host of challenges, including issues related to ownership, sponsorship and logistics.The upcoming edition could face further uncertainty as there are talks about a couple of franchises opting out.
Article Summary: Dilip Tirkey is currently in the Netherlands for the FIH World Cup. Questions have been raised about the HI president's absence from the tournament. Tirkey told TOI that he would not travel for the World Cup because of the next edition of the Hockey India League (HIL)

Article Title: Ajaraie’s hat-trick stuns Shillong Lajong as NorthEast United reach Durand Cup semis
Article Text:
NEUFC’s Alaaeddine Ajaraie after scoring at JLN Stadium in Shillong on Monday (Image Credit: NEUFC)

KOLKATA: Till the 55th minute of the quarterfinal at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Shillong on Monday, Shillong Lajong were in control of the game, holding a one-goal lead with a festive crowd in the stands backing them.However, it all changed and swiftly went downhill for them after Etyan Gonzalez found the equaliser for NorthEast United FC from an Alaaeddine Ajaraie assist to make it 2-2. The defending champions then got into their rhythm, with Ajaraie, who had given them the breakthrough in the 11th minute, adding two more goals in the 58th and 69th minutes to complete his second hat-trick of the 135th Durand Cup.Jithin MS, who had assisted Ajaraie for his third goal, then completed the rout with a goal of his own in the 79th minute, making Shillong Lajong’s first-half strikes from Figo Syndai (20’) and Jota (34’) count for little.NEUFC set up a semifinal against Mohun Bagan Super Giant, who defeated Jamshedpur FC in a penalty shootout in the earlier quarterfinal at Birsa Munda Football Stadium in Ranchi.The Red Miners held the most successful club in the competition to a 1-1 draw at the end of regulation time at the Slat Lake Stadium in Kolkata, after which the two sides traded 16 successful penalties before Jamshedpur faltered when Lawmsangzuala missed. Takchim Abhishek Singh then converted the next kick to earn Bagan a place in the last four of Asia’s oldest football tournament.Earlier, Sahal Abdul Samad got the breakthrough for the Kolkata giants in the second minute before Devendra Murgaonkar equalised at the stroke of the 45th minute.

Article Title: Rishabh Pant’s Test brilliance refuses to fade, but can he force his way back into India’s 2027 ODI World Cup plans?
Article Text:
Galle: India's Rishabh Pant loses his balance while playing a shot on day four (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The past year has proved to be the toughest phase of Rishabh Pant ’s eventful career. After a second successive underwhelming IPL season, where he scored just 312 runs in 14 matches at 28.36, Pant lost the Lucknow Super Giants captaincy and returned to Delhi Capitals. His troubles extended beyond the IPL.He slipped out of India’s ODI plans, even missing out on the reserve wicketkeeper’s spot to Ishan Kishan, and lost Test vice-captaincy to KL Rahul.Yet, whenever Pant dons the whites, everything seems to change.For all his ups and downs in limited-overs cricket, Pant continues to be one of India’s most impactful Test cricketers. Before this Test, the 28-year-old had scored 3,557 runs in 50 Tests at an average of 43.37, with eight hundreds and 19 fifties. Few wicketkeeper-batters in world cricket can match that record.His love affair with Test cricket began fittingly on Aug 18, 2018, when he announced himself by smashing a six off England’s Adil Rashid with his second ball in Tests at Nottingham. Eight years to the day, Pant was at it again, becoming the first Indian and the fastest batter to hit 100 Test sixes while playing another innings that underlined why he is one of India’s biggest match-winners.The knock also revives an intriguing question: Can India really afford to leave Pant out of their plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia?His ODI numbers are modest, 871 runs in 31 matches at 33.50 with one century and five fifties, but Pant possesses the ability to change games in a session.“He’s a pure match-winner. If he has smashed 100 sixes in red-ball cricket, he can be dangerous in white-ball cricket too,” former India keeper and chief selector Kiran More told TOI.On Tuesday, Pant once again demonstrated that game-changing ability. With India searching for quick runs and momentum on Day Four of the rain-hit first Test at Galle, he blasted a 69-ball 66 that tilted the contest decisively in the visitors’ favour.Pant dominated a 54-run seventh-wicket stand with Ravindra Jadeja , who contributed just eight runs. His innings featured the audacity and flair that have become his trademark. The pick of his shots was a sensational charge down the track to Lahiru Kumara before slapping the ball over wide mid-off for six. It was a stroke few would attempt.His rapid 20th Test fifty helped India set Sri Lanka a daunting 372-run target and ensured the hosts remained under pressure.Teammate Devdutt Padikkal, who scored 167 in the first innings, summed up Pant’s value best. “It’s great entertainment. He is one of those batters you love to watch every day of the week. He really took the game to them and put them under pressure. That’s the ability he has.He can win games on his own. Everyone is really happy to have a player like him in our side,” he said.Pant’s second six off Kumara got him the 100th six.At a time when questions continue to surround his white-ball future, on Tuesday Pant served a reminder that genuine match-winners are rare. Every time doubts begin to surface, he finds a way to answer them. And if his Test exploits are any indication, leaving him out of India’s 2027 World Cup plans may prove far harder than it currently seems.
Article Summary: Rishabh Pant becomes the first Indian and the fastest batter to hit 100 Test sixes. His rapid 20th Test fifty helped India set Sri Lanka a daunting 372-run target. Pant dominated a 54-run seventh-wicket stand with Ravindra Jadeja.

Article Title: Rishabh Pant’s 100th six, Manav Suthar’s double strike put India on brink of Galle victory
Article Text:
India's Manav Suthar, second right, celebrates with teammates (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Buoyed by a sizzling half-century from Rishabh Pant , during which he became the first Indian and the fastest batter to smash 100 sixes in Test cricket, and with their bowlers causing telling dents in the hosts’ line-up, India have begun their charge towards victory in the first Test at Galle. A win would keep them firmly in the race for a spot in the final of the 2027 World Test Championship.After setting Lanka a target of 372, India’s bowlers, briefly halted by a short shower, came out breathing fire. Pacers Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna took a wicket each, while left-arm spinner Manav Suthar again looked dangerous in the spin-friendly conditions, taking two for 30. Suthar now has match figures of six for 106 in his first away Test.Suffering another top-order malfunction, Sri Lanka slipped to 47 for four before finishing the day at 84 for four in 34 overs. Skipper Dhananjaya de Silva was unbeaten on 31 (73b, 3x4), with first-innings centurion Sonal Dinusha (25 not out, 36b, 4x4) giving him company.India need six more wickets to wrap up the Test on Day Five, while Lanka require another 288 runs, an improbable task considering Pakistan’s 344 for six in 2022 remains the highest successful fourth-innings chase at Galle.Opener Nishan Madhushka Fernando (6 off 27 balls) succumbed to the short-ball trap as he hooked a Siraj bouncer to a diving Krishna at deep fine leg in the seventh over.No. 3 Pasindu Sooriyabandara, making his Test debut as concussion substitute for the injured Dinesh Chandimal, was trapped lbw first ball by Suthar. The left-arm spinner’s delivery came in with the arm and struck him on the back leg.Earlier, Chandimal was taken to hospital for a precautionary scan and was subsequently replaced by Sooriyabandara, who had taken Ravindra Jadeja’s catch.Bowling with verve and generating good pace, Krishna struck in his first over, having Kamindu Mendis (2) poking at a delivery outside off and edging it to KL Rahul at first slip.In fact, Lanka would have been four down earlier but for a big reprieve for captain Dhananjaya de Silva, who was on seven when he was caught at first slip off Ravindra Jadeja in the 16th over. Jadeja had overstepped, however, and the wicket did not count.Rescued by Pant’s fifty after slipping to 120 for five, India were all out for 193, leaving the hosts with a 372-run target.The highlight of Pant’s impactful knock (66, 69b, 8x4, 2x6) was an audacious six he hit after stepping out to greet pacer Lahiru Kumara in the 27th over of India’s second innings. Sailing over wide long-off, the ball landed on the road outside.Pant later pulled Kumara for another six to bring up his 20th Test fifty. It was also his landmark 100th six in Tests.Sri Lanka’s chief wicket-takers were pacer Asitha Fernando (four for 31 in 8.5 overs) and left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya (three for 43 in 11 overs).Opener Yashasvi Jaiswal fell for a three-ball duck, edging a cut off Fernando to wicketkeeper Niroshan Dickwella in the first over. The left-hander has managed just one fifty in his last eight Test innings.Gill was dismissed cheaply by Jayasuriya for the second time in the match, falling lbw while attempting a sweep. But first-innings centurion Devdutt Padikkal (44, 75b, 6x4) and KL Rahul (35, 47b, 2x4, 2x6) made useful contributions.After Jaiswal’s early dismissal, Padikkal and Rahul added 65 in 87 balls for the second wicket. Using his feet well, Rahul clubbed Jayasuriya for two fine sixes.He also survived a close lbw call off Jayasuriya on 25. The on-field umpire’s decision was overturned on review after ball-tracking showed it would have gone over the stumps. The reprieve did not last long, though, as Rahul holed out off Jayasuriya, with substitute fielder RMMP Rathnayaka taking the catch at deep mid-off.Padikkal then hit sublime drives through extra cover and used the sweep and loft to collect boundaries off Nuwantha.
Article Summary: India need six more wickets to wrap up the Test on Day Five. Lanka require another 288 runs, an improbable task considering Pakistan’s 344 for six in 2022 remains the highest successful fourth-innings chase at Galle. Rishabh Pant became the first Indian and fastest batter to smash 100 sixes in Test cricket.

Article Title: Pakistan suffer major blow as captain Babar Azam ruled out of first Test against England
Article Text:
Babar Azam

Babar ruled out, Agha takes charge

England also enter new era

Pakistan suffer a major setback ahead of the first Test against England as newly reappointed captain Babar Azam is ruled out with a finger injury. Babar injures the middle finger of his right hand while batting against the West Indies and aggravates it during a warm-up game in Beckenham.“Pakistan captain Babar Azam is unavailable for the first test match,” Pakistan coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said. “Salman Agha will be the captain for the first test.”Ahmed confirms that Babar’s finger is not broken but says the team hopes the pain settles in time for the second Test at Lord’s, starting August 27. Babar’s absence is a significant blow after he recently returned as captain and was Pakistan’s leading run-scorer against the West Indies.Agha is set to captain Pakistan in a Test for the first time, having already led the team in T20 cricket. Shan Masood, who was replaced by Babar as captain, also returns after recovering from a broken finger.“Our practice match gave us a lot of confidence,” Ahmed said. “Whatever bases we needed to cover with bat and ball, we did. We believe we'll do very well here.”England, meanwhile, begin the series under a changed leadership setup. Joe Root returns as captain following Ben Stokes’ retirement, while Brendon McCullum has also left the coaching role. Marcus Trescothick takes interim charge as new coach Stephen Fleming misses the series.Root, who previously led England from 2017 to 2022, says his experience has prepared him for another stint as captain.“I feel as ready as any other England captain that's ever been before,” Root said. “To have that amount of experience is invaluable.”Harry Brook remains vice-captain, with Root confident of his support.“I fully feel he's got my back like the rest of the guys do,” Root said.

Pakistan coach Sarfaraz Ahmed confirms that Babar’s finger is not broken but says the team hopes the pain settles in time for the second Test at Lord's.

Article Title: 'We had to make sure to put pressure back on them': Devdutt Padikkal after India ends Day 4 on top
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal (Photo by Sahil Malhotra/TimesofIndia.com)

Padikkal on red-ball adjustments

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India eye victory in Galle

NEW DELHI: Devdutt Padikkal believes India’s aggressive approach and a strong showing from the fast bowlers have put the team in a commanding position heading into the final day of the first Test against Sri Lanka at Galle.India closed Day 4 with Sri Lanka struggling at 84-4, still needing 288 runs to reach the imposing target of 372. Padikkal, who scored 44 in India’s second innings, said the team was conscious of the need to regain control after losing wickets while chasing quick runs.“We had to make sure to put pressure back on them with quick runs to establish control again,” Padikkal said during the post-day press conference.India was bowled out for 193 in 48.5 overs after beginning the day at 54-2. Rishabh Pant provided the biggest push, scoring 66 off 69 balls, while Padikkal contributed 44 off 75 and KL Rahul made 35 off 47. India then made early inroads into Sri Lanka’s chase.Mohammed Siraj removed Nishan Madushka for six before Manav Suthar struck twice. Prasidh Krishna later dismissed Kamindu Mendis, leaving Sri Lanka at 47-4 before Dhananjaya de Silva and Sonal Dinusha survived the final hour.Padikkal also spoke about the technical changes he has been working on as he adapts between white-ball and Test cricket.“Worked on lot of things. Technique changes from white ball to red ball. I have a setup for whiteball but its important to tighten with my hands being closer for the red ball. I have gotten better at it and hopefully can keep getting better,” he said.With the No.3 spot likely to remain a talking point, Padikkal praised Sai Sudharsan, who has also been competing for a place in India’s top order.“Sai has been doing well for us, very talented. Whoever gets that opportunity, should do well,” Padikkal said.He also spoke positively about his partnership with Rahul, saying the two understand each other's game well.“Batting with him enjoyable, we have had long partnerships. We play well with each other, he understands my tempo. Such chemistry helps,” he said.Padikkal also reserved praise for Pant, whose attacking 66 helped India push the scoring rate and build a sizeable lead.“Great entertainment, he produces moments. Puts them under pressure. Everyone is happy to have a player like him in the side,” Padikkal said.Padikkal was impressed by India’s pace attack, particularly given the conditions in Galle. He said the pitch has begun offering more assistance to the spinners as the Test progresses.“Fast bowlers bowled really well. Didnt expect fast bowlers to pick those many wickets but we know match moves really quickly in Galle Day 3/4 onwards. Pitch is turning more from the stumps now, than it was earlier. It is turning a lot more now.”With Sri Lanka needing 288 more runs and India six wickets away from victory, the final day promises a tense finish.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal believes India's aggressive approach and fast bowlers have put the team in a commanding position. India closed Day 4 with Sri Lanka struggling at 84-4, still needing 288 runs to reach the imposing target of 372. India was bowled out for 193 in 48.5 overs after beginning the day at 54-2. Rishabh Pant provided the biggest push, scoring 66 off 69 balls.

Brief Scores

Sri Lanka:

KL Rahul reluctantly stood his ground after the umpire raised his finger. Prabath Jayasuriya was convinced, the close-in fielders were celebrating, but Devdutt Padikkal, at the non-striker's end, pushed his senior teammate to ask for a review. The right-hander pointed towards his back leg, but the moment replays confirmed contact with the front pad, it looked curtains. Then, the seven-letter word, 'missing,' flashed, and Rahul gave Padikkal a warm hug.The review and the moment left mixed tastes and contrasting reactions, but with a similar degree of surprise from both the batter and Sri Lanka players, which aptly summed up the situation as focus moved back to live action. The ongoing Galle Test has had anything but an expected storyline. Who would have thought that 14 wickets would fall on Day 4, with eight of those picked up by the fast bowlers from both sides?Not just that, when India were expected to bat Sri Lanka out of the contest, they failed to do so. The hosts' early collapse made the writing on the wall clearer, but the rearguard rescue act changed the mood. And just when India looked favoured to return to the "bat out of the game" narrative, an ordinary batting performance never allowed the declaration question to get louder as the visitors were bundled out for just 193 in 48.5 overs.The sun was out in its full glory on Day 4, and the clear sky meant we had an extended period of uninterrupted cricket at hand.Brisk runs were the need of the hour, but Yashasvi Jaiswal's dismissal off just the third delivery of the innings set the tone for the remainder. The left-hander chased an early delivery, Rahul perished after an ordinary shot, Shubman Gill continued to bat in a very un-Gill-like fashion, and except for Devdutt Padikkal and Rishabh Pant, no other India batter showed the stomach for a fight. India looked to re-establish control in the Test with quick runs but chose questionable shots in the process."We had to make sure to put pressure back on them with quick runs to establish control again," said Devdutt Padikkal, centurion of the first innings, at the end of the day's play on Tuesday.The pitch wasn't raging or turning square, and conditions remained ideal for batting. However, the cushion of the lead seemed to allow complacency and carelessness to creep into the second innings. Jaiswal should have done better; Rahul could have opted for a different approach against Prabath Jayasuriya; Gill opted for a shot he doesn't play often, and in no time, India had three of the top four with their feet up in the dressing room.If not for Padikkal's fluency and Rishabh Pant's fight, India could have been in a precarious situation, as only three batters reached double digits. Pant stood out with his audacious strokeplay, as he has on numerous occasions in the past. The bowlers played with his mind by setting different traps, but the left-hander continued to find a way through, scoring boundaries. He would charge down the ground and play a tennis-like forehand, and the next ball, he would go deep in his crease to play one fine. He used sweeps and reverse-sweeps to full effect, focusing on only one currency: runs. And no matter how they came.Pant isn't for the faint-hearted, and neither is his wagon wheel, but one constant remains: the ability to boss tricky situations, even if it keeps everyone on the edge of their seat. He didn't get any support from the other end but fought a lonely battle before the short-ball trap finally worked for Sri Lanka, who were tactically sharp with their bowling changes and field placements."Yeah, it's great entertainment. I think he is one of those batters who you love to watch every day of the week. And he produces moments like he did today. He really took the game to them and put them under a lot of pressure. I think that's the ability that he has. He can win games on his own. And when something like that comes off, I think it's always great to watch. And I think everyone is really happy to have a player like him in our side," added Padikkal.Pant was fearless, but the hosts came prepared with different plans for every batter. They used their seamers Asitha Fernando and Lahiru Kumara very smartly, and the pair returned with a collective six wickets. The last instance of seamers together picking five or more wickets at this venue was back in 2016, when Mitchell Starc took six and Josh Hazlewood took one."To be honest, we didn't really expect the fast bowlers to pick all those wickets. That did fall today, I think. But at the same time, credit goes to the fast bowlers. They really put a lot of effort in. They bowled some good spells and they have really done a good job. But at the end of the day, I think the goal you expect from the third day onwards for the game to quicken up a little bit, I think it definitely did turn a little bit more."Especially today, it started turning a little bit more off the stumps. I think initially, it was turning probably from the fourth stump and now it is starting to turn from the stumps as well. For us, as a team, trying to get 10 wickets, that is a really good sign. Hopefully, tomorrow it continues to deteriorate a little bit," explained Padikkal.Sri Lanka fast bowling coach Ryan van Niekerk lavished praise on the pair of Asitha Fernando and Lahiru Kumara for bringing the hosts back into the game from a challenging position, asserting that being proactive helped them find answers."There have been ebbs and flows in this Test, but the bowling group has been very proactive. We had plans and credit goes to the bowlers for executing them. Asitha has been doing a great job for us, and Lahiru cracked open the game with that spell where he brought so much energy," said Ryan."Historically, we know a lot of wickets fall in Galle from Day 4 onwards, so I wasn't surprised by that," he further added.The start to the mammoth 372-run chase wasn't ideal for Sri Lanka as they lost four quick wickets and faced the heat in the final session of the day's play. India were spot on with their tactics, and the ploy of hunting in pairs with spin and pace worked. Mohammed Siraj and Manav Suthar set the ball rolling, and Prasidh Krishna and Ravindra Jadeja sustained the pressure as the first-change pair. While Suthar continued to get a lot of turn, Prasidh bowled with a lot of heat in the fading light to keep the hosts under the pump.Sri Lanka will need a special effort to score 288 runs on the final day, and it's now up to the Indian bowlers to take the remaining six wickets to not only conquer the Galle challenge but also leave a satisfying taste in the mouth when they leave the coastal city. The script, just like the weather, has been anything but predictable, but India wouldn't mind riding the ebbs and flows for one last time.462 & 193 (Rishabh Pant 62, Devdutt Padikkal 44; Asitha Fernando 4/31, Prabath Jayasuriya 3/43, Lahiru Kumara 2/28)284 & 84/4 (Dhananjaya de Silva 31 batting, Sonal Dinusha 25 batting; Manav Suthar 2/30, Mohammed Siraj 1/11)
Article Summary: 14 wickets fall on Day 4, with eight of those picked up by the fast bowlers from both sides. India were expected to bat Sri Lanka out of the contest, they failed to do so. The hosts' early collapse made the writing on the wall clearer, but the rearguard rescue act changed the mood.

Article Title: IND vs SL 1st Test: India on verge of massive win as Sri Lanka four down in chase of 372
Article Text:
Team India (BCCI Photo)

Suthar, Prasidh rip through Sri Lanka's top order

Pant's 66 gives India commanding position

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India moved to the brink of a massive victory in the first Test against Sri Lanka after their bowlers produced a ruthless final session to reduce the hosts to 84 for four at stumps on Tuesday, leaving them 288 runs short of an improbable 372-run target.India had earlier stretched their lead with a counter-attacking second innings, posting 193 after Rishabh Pant's typically audacious 66, Devdutt Padikkal's 44 and KL Rahul's 35 provided crucial runs. With only six wickets standing, Sri Lanka face a daunting final day against an Indian attack that has already made significant inroads.Captain Dhananjaya de Silva was unbeaten on 31 at the close, with Sonal Dinusha, who scored a century in the first innings, on 25. But the scale of the task facing Sri Lanka is reflected by Galle's history. The highest successful fourth-innings chase at the venue is Pakistan's 344 in 2022, while a target above 200 has been chased successfully only twice at the ground since 1998.Sri Lanka's chase began after a brief rain interruption, but the hosts looked immediately under pressure. Mohammed Siraj hurried Nishan Fernando into a pull shot, which he failed to control, allowing Prasidh Krishna to take the catch in the deep.Prasidh then struck again to remove Kamindu Mendis. After sending three deliveries into the left-hander, the pacer shaped one away and Mendis edged it to KL Rahul in the cordon.In between those wickets, left-arm spinner Manav Suthar accounted for Pasindu Sooriyabandara, who had replaced Dinesh Chandimal as a concussion substitute. Chandimal had struck his shoulder and head on the ground while fielding earlier in the day. Although his scan showed no injury, he was unable to clear the concussion test.Sooriyabandara's introduction to Test cricket lasted just one delivery as Suthar trapped him leg before wicket. The spinner later added Lahiru Udara to his tally, leaving Sri Lanka in deep trouble.Earlier, Sri Lanka's bowlers had exploited the conditions well and picked up wickets at regular intervals, but Padikkal and Pant ensured India could establish a sizeable lead.Pant produced another trademark counter-attacking innings, reaching his half-century from just 53 balls. He brought up the landmark with a six off Lahiru Kumara and added 54 runs with Ravindra Jadeja.The six also took Pant to 100 sixes in Test cricket, making him the first Indian and the fastest batter to reach the landmark.Pant's innings eventually ended when he nicked Kumara behind to wicketkeeper Niroshan Dickwella, but his contribution had already transformed India's position.Padikkal, who had scored 167 in the first innings, continued his excellent match with a fluent 44. He attacked the spinners with sweeps, cuts and drives before Keshara Nuwantha trapped him on the back foot.India had begun their second innings shakily, with Yashasvi Jaiswal edging Asitha Fernando in the opening over. Rahul then steadied the innings and attacked Prabath Jayasuriya with two sixes before falling to the spinner after a 65-run partnership with Padikkal.Shubman Gill also fell to Jayasuriya, trapped leg before, before Pant and Padikkal helped India build the decisive advantage.
Article Summary: Rishabh Pant's 66 gives India commanding position against Sri Lanka. Devdutt Padikkal's 44 and KL Rahul's 35 provide crucial runs. Sri Lanka face daunting final day against an Indian attack that has already made significant inroads.

Article Title: ‘That’s a bad one’: Sanjay Manjrekar, Murali Kartik’s on-air banter turns ugly - Watch

Article Title: David Warner convicted and fined for drink-driving; Sydney Thunder captaincy under cloud
Article Text:

Court stresses need to deter drink-driving

Former Australia opener David Warner has been convicted of mid-range drink-driving by a Sydney court and fined AUD 1,500, with the 39-year-old also required to have an interlock device fitted to his vehicle before he can drive again.Warner pleaded guilty to the charge last month after he was caught in a random breath test on Easter Sunday, April 5. The former Test opener had stopped short of a roadside testing site and attempted to switch seats with a female passenger before police identified him as the driver.Warner subsequently cooperated with the testing and blew more than twice the legal alcohol limit.The incident has also cast doubt over his position as captain of Sydney Thunder ahead of the upcoming Big Bash League season. Thunder, along with Sydney Sixers and Sheffield Shield side NSW Blues, are part of a state government campaign aimed at discouraging drink-driving.Warner's barrister, Awais Ahmad, argued that his client should be spared a conviction because the incident had already resulted in significant consequences, including widespread media coverage.Ahmad told Waverley Local Court that Warner's case had been reported by international outlets including ESPN and Al Jazeera.He also pointed to the potential impact on Warner's commercial opportunities, particularly in countries such as India and Bangladesh where he could seek opportunities in T20 franchise leagues."The consequences of his offending are profound," Ahmad said. "Commercial opportunities (are) being affected."The lawyer also questioned why NSW Police had issued a press release about Warner's arrest, describing the subsequent coverage as excessive."The media onslaught thereafter has been quite profound," he said.Warner was arrested while returning home from Pakistan, where he had captained Karachi Kings in the Pakistan Super League, before returning to resume his campaign.Judge Clare Farnan acknowledged the impact of the publicity, saying there was evidence of cruel social media commentary directed at Warner and his wife Candice Warner.However, she said deterrence remained paramount in deciding to convict Warner, particularly because children were in the vehicle at the time of the offence."I accept Mr Warner is unlikely to reoffend," Farnan said. "(But) regrettably, drink-driving is still a significant factor in many crashes in NSW."The judge noted that more than 17,300 people had appeared before the court for mid-range drink-driving offences over the previous five years.Warner will be able to drive once he applies for an interlock licence and has the device fitted to his car. The technology prevents a vehicle from starting if it detects alcohol in the driver's system.Cricket NSW acknowledged the sentence and said it continued "to take the incident seriously, including educating all players on the importance of safe driving".
Article Summary: David Warner convicted of mid-range drink-driving by a Sydney court. Former Australia opener fined AUD 1,500 and required to have interlock device fitted to his vehicle. Warner pleaded guilty to the charge last month after he was caught in a random breath test on Easter Sunday, April 5.

Article Title: 18 years of ruthless Virat Kohli: The man who refused to stay ordinary
Article Text:
18 years of Virat Kohli (AI Genarated Image)

The boy who learned early that cricket could not wait

The World Cup, Tendulkar and the making of a star

The chase master tag

Captain Kohli: India stopped apologising

2016: Kohli became the real beast

2018: The captain who conquered overseas cricket

And then came the fall

The comeback began with 122*

2023: The year he chased history

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai: India's Virat Kohli celebrates his 50th century, breaking Sachin Tendulkar's most ODI hundreds record, during the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 semi-final match between India and New Zealand, at the Wankhede Stadium, in Mumbai. (PTI Photo/Kunal Patil)

And then, finally, Bengaluru gave him his closure

On August 18, 2008, a 19-year-old Virat Kohli walked out at Dambulla and scored 12 on his India debut. Eighteen years later, the boy who was once a surprise selection has become one of the defining figures of modern cricket: a batter, captain, standard-setter, survivor and, perhaps most importantly, a player who changed what Indian cricket expected from itself.Virat Kohli is not just an athlete; he has become a brand of cricket, inspiring a generation through his mindset, skills and, most importantly, his hunger for the game. That hunger made him more intense, more furious and, at his best, almost unbeatable. Across his career, Kohli has achieved almost everything: the U19 World Cup, ODI World Cup, T20 World Cup, Champions Trophy and Asia Cup.There was nothing particularly prophetic about Virat Kohli's first international innings.On that day at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium in Sri Lanka, the teenager walked out to open India's innings. He faced 22 balls, made 12 and was trapped lbw by Nuwan Kulasekara.India lost by eight wickets. There was no century. No match-winning chase. No hint, at least in the scorecard, that something extraordinary had begun.Eighteen years later, the numbers have become difficult to ignore.As of August 2026, Kohli has played 314 ODIs and scored 14,941 runs at 58.59, with 54 hundreds and 79 fifties.He has 9,230 Test runs from 123 matches, including 30 centuries, and finished his T20I career with 4,188 runs from 125 matches. Across international cricket, that is 28,359 runs and 85 centuries.Long before Dambulla, there was a December morning in 2006 that revealed something about Kohli that statistics never could. He was 18, playing for Delhi against Karnataka in a Ranji Trophy match at the Feroz Shah Kotla. He was unbeaten on 40 overnight when his father, Prem Kohli, died suddenly. Kohli returned to the ground the next morning. He scored 90. It was not just an innings. It was an early declaration of character.Two years later, he was leading India at the Under-19 World Cup in Malaysia. India won the tournament. Kohli scored 235 runs in six innings at an average of 47.He had a modest start to his international career during the Sri Lanka tour. In the fourth ODI of that 2008 series, Kohli made 54, his first international half-century. A year later came his first hundred: 107 against Sri Lanka in Kolkata.By 2011, Kohli was no longer a prospect. He was part of India's World Cup-winning side. He scored a century against Bangladesh in India's opening game and later walked into the Wankhede dressing room during the final when India were 31 for 2.He made 35. Not the sort of number that usually survives in a career built on hundreds. His 35 helped India recover alongside Gautam Gambhir, before MS Dhoni's 91 finished the job against Sri Lanka.India won the World Cup. Kohli was just 22.The 2012 Asia Cup against Pakistan produced his famous 183, still his highest ODI score. The same year brought a defining chase in Hobart against Sri Lanka, where India needed 321 in 40 overs to stay alive in the tournament. Kohli smashed 133 not out from 86 balls.MS Dhoni stepped down as captain in Test cricket in 2014 and in limited-overs formats in 2017. Kohli was handed the captaincy, first in Tests in 2015 and then across formats by 2017. From then on, India began to excel in the longest format. The early signs were visible in Australia in 2014-15. Kohli scored hundreds in both innings of the Adelaide Test, making 115 and 141.Kohli soon took India from No. 7 to the No. 1 Test team in the world.If 2014-15 established Kohli as a great, 2016 turned him into a sporting phenomenon. He was devastating in every format. Then came the IPL. 973 runs in 16 matches. Four centuries. An average of 81.08. It was a season that seemed to break the accepted limits of T20 batting. Kohli was no longer simply a successful cricketer.The fitness. The diet. The running between wickets. The hunger after reaching fifty. Young Indian cricketers began copying Kohli's routines because they understood the larger message: talent could get you into the team, but obsession could keep you there.The 2018 season cemented the Test version of Kohli. He scored 1,322 Test runs and was named ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year.India had always produced great batters. Kohli wanted India to produce great fast bowlers. Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Shami, Ishant Sharma and Umesh Yadav became the spearhead of an attack that could win Test matches away from home. The defining reward came in Australia in 2018-19, when India won their first Test series on Australian soil.Kohli finished with 68 Tests as captain, 40 wins and 17 defeats, the most Test victories by an Indian captain and the fourth-most in the history of Test cricket.From November 2019 to March 2023, Kohli went through 23 Tests and 41 innings without a Test century, averaging only 25.70 during that stretch. His 70th international century came in November 2019.The 71st did not arrive until September 2022, 1,020 days later. In 2021, Kohli stepped down from captaincy, and then he made his comeback.At the 2022 Asia Cup, Kohli finally looked free again. Against Afghanistan, he made 122 not out from 61 balls, his first T20I century and his 71st international hundred. Then came Pakistan at the 2022 T20 World Cup. India needed 160. Kohli made 82 not out from 53 balls.It was not simply another great innings. It was the kind of performance that reminded everyone why his name had become synonymous with pressure.At the ODI World Cup in India, Kohli produced one of the greatest individual tournament campaigns in the history of the competition.765 runs in 11 innings. Average: 95.63. He became the first player to score 50 ODI hundreds, surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's record of 49.He then won back-to-back ICC trophies, the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 Champions Trophy. The following year he retired from Test cricket and T20Is, leaving behind a long-lasting legacy.There was one unfinished story left. Royal Challengers Bengaluru. Kohli had been there since the first IPL season in 2008. He had watched the franchise lose finals in 2009, 2011 and 2016. He had carried the weight of an entire fanbase through years of disappointment. Then, in 2025, RCB finally won the IPL. And in 2026, they did it again.Kohli completed his chapter of cricket with every major trophy and countless individual awards to his name. As of August 2026, Kohli is no longer a Test cricketer. He is no longer a T20I cricketer. He is now an ODI specialist for India - still scoring, still competing.
Article Summary: On August 18, 2008, a 19-year-old Virat Kohli walked out at Dambulla and scored 12 on his India debut. Eighteen years later, the boy who was once a surprise selection has become one of the defining figures of modern cricket. Kohli is not just an athlete; he has become a brand of cricket.

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest.
